With adversus, . —

Affirmatively, to take care for, attend to a thing for a person, provide: Ba. Haec ita me orat sibi qui caveat aliquem ut hominem reperiam... Id, amabo te, huic caveas. Pi. Quid isti caveam? ; ; cf. I. C. 3. supra.—Hence, cautus, a, um, P. a.
Neutr., careful, circumspect, wary, cautious, provident (syn.: providus, prudens; class. in prose and poetry): ut cautus est, ubi nihil opu'st,: parum cauti providique,: cauti in periculis,: in scribendo,: in credendo,: in verbis serendis,: mensor,: mariti,: lupus,: vulpes, et saep.: quem certi homines monuerunt, ut cautior esset,: dubium cautior an audentior,.—Constr. with ad: ad praesentius malum cautiores,; ; . —With adversus: parum cautus adversus colloquii fraudem,.—With erga: erga bona sua satis cautus,.—With contra: contra quam (fortunam) non satis cauta mortalitas est,.—With inf.: cautum dignos assumere,.—With gen.: rei divinae,.—
Transf. to inanimate things: consilium,; : cautissima senectus,: pectus,manus,: terga,: arma,: timor,.—Subst.: cauta, ōrum, n.: legum,the provisions,.—
Pass. (acc. to I. B. 1., and II. B.), made safe, secured: cautos nominibus rectis expendere nummos,: cautus ab incursu belli,: quo mulieri esset res cautior (that her property might be made more secure), curavit, ut, etc., .—
Trop., safe, secure (rare): in eam partem peccare, quae est cautior,: (civitates) murorum firmitate cautissimae,.—Adv.: cau-tē.
(Acc. to caveo, I. A.) Cautiously: caute et cogitate rem tractare,: pedetentimque dicere,: et cum judicio, et saep. —Comp., ; ; ; —Sup., .—
(Acc. to caveo, I. B. 1.) With security, cautiously, : aliter nec caute nec jure fieri potest,.
